_comment: PLAT-35 — THE SCENARIO DEFINITION. IT NAMES NO RENDERER.
Cross-Renderer-Visual-Alignment.md §4: 'A scenario names a recording, a
sequence of debugger operations, a viewport and a view name; it does not
name a renderer.' One definition, two capture paths.
WHY JSON AND NOT A NIM CONST. The two capture paths are written in two
languages: the GPUI side is Nim and the Electron side is TypeScript under
Playwright. A Nim const would have to be transcribed into TypeScript, and a
transcription is a second copy of one definition — Verification-Harness-Traps
§30 arriving through a file copy. One file, two readers, no copy.
THE SCENARIO SET IS PINNED AND ITS CARDINALITY IS ASSERTED, the same way
PLAT-31's task set and PLAT-34's sequence corpus are. `expectedScenarios`
below is read by both readers and compared against the parsed length, so a
parser that stopped early cannot pass.
STEPPED BEFORE CAPTURE. PLAT-23 measured why: a Python program at line 1
genuinely has no locals, and its pane census moved from locals=0 to locals=8
on that one change — two empty screens compare equal. Five of the six
scenarios are stepped. The sixth, `entry-shell`, is deliberately NOT, and it
is the POPULATION CONTROL rather than an oversight: the suite asserts that
its answers DIFFER from every other scenario's.
THE SIX REACH SIX DIFFERENT PROGRAM STATES, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF
THE SET. Verification-Harness-Traps §34 is the trap this is written against:
a scenario set whose members are structurally identical makes the comparison
vacuous — eight questions times six copies of one screen is eight cases
wearing a multiplier. So no two scenarios share an operation sequence: one
is unstepped, one is six frames in, one is six frames in and three
statements along, one has returned a frame, one has run to completion, and
one carries a gutter mark. The suite asserts the six answer sets are
PAIRWISE DISTINCT and fails if they are not.
THE OPERATION VOCABULARY IS CLOSED. Five members, every one of which both
drivers can perform: the GPUI driver through `HeadlessDebugSession`, the
Electron driver through the product's own debug-toolbar buttons. An op no
driver can perform is a scenario that silently captures a different state on
one side.
THE VIEWPORT MATRIX IS EXERCISED BY THE SET RATHER THAN DECLARED BESIDE IT.
Two of the six sit at `laptop`, so the normalised-coordinate claim in
question one — that a rectangle is reported in hundredths of the viewport —
has scenarios at two viewports to be wrong at.
`gpuiProbes` IS A SECOND ARRAY AND NOT A SEVENTH SCENARIO, 2026-10-03,
AND THE REASON IS MEASURED RATHER THAN STYLISTIC. PLAT-35's `PLAT35-F14`
needed an UNSTEPPED breakpoint case: `breakpoint-editor` is
`stepIn=5, setBreakpoint@1` and `setBreakpoint@<row>` is an offset into
the editor's FIRST DRAWN ROW, which after five stepIns is 31 — so its mark
always lands on a two-digit row and that scenario CANNOT fail the finding.
Reproducing it took an ad-hoc command line, and an assertion that cannot
fail is the defect this campaign is about.
Growing `scenarios` to seven was measured first and refused, because FOUR
other milestones pin the six and TWO of them pin it against a record this
host cannot regenerate:
* `screen_oracle/test_screen_oracle.nim` — `ck Scenarios.len == 6` and
`declared.toHashSet == Scenarios.toHashSet` against PLAT-39's own
`plat39_record.Scenarios` const;
* `screen_oracle/test_plat39_record.nim` — the recorded cardinality
against this file's, BOTH WAYS, over
`src/tests/visual/plat39-readings.json`,
which only `just plat39-record` writes and which needs the Electron
captures (Xvfb) and the OCR stack;
* `gpui/tests/test_gpui_window_frame.nim` — `ck expectedScenarios == 6`;
* `gpui/tests/plat38_keys.nim` — `PinnedScenarioCount* = 6`.
A seventh member would redden PLAT-39 in a commit that cannot re-record
it, which `ci/test/plat37-window-frame.sh` already states as a rule of
this corpus: *"NO SEVENTH SCENARIO. The six come from
`src/tests/visual/scenarios.json`, unchanged and un-renamed … a scenario
invented for this milestone would be a corpus that grew to fit its
instrument."*
So the probes are a SEPARATE, SEPARATELY COUNTED array with the same
shape and the same closed operation vocabulary, read by the GPUI arm
only — `ci/test/plat35-gpui-capture.sh` captures them after the six and
`gpui/tests/test_plat35_gutter_lanes.nim` asserts that an unstepped
breakpoint case is among them. The precedent for the GPUI arm covering a
different set is `plat39_record.GpuiScenarios`, which is two of the six.
A probe is NOT part of the cross-renderer comparison: it has no Electron
arm, so nothing here claims one.

scenarios.why: The population control. Not stepped, so the panes hold what a session holds at entry. Without it nothing says the five stepped scenarios are not five copies of one screen.

Dense text, five steps in: line 44, the stop `test_cross_renderer_panes.nim` once measured as the one that fills all four panes. FIVE SINCE 2026-10-04, and the stop is unchanged: the engine now opens a recording in the program's entry call, `<__main__>` at line 1, rather than on the `<toplevel>` root's synthetic entry step one step earlier at the same line (codetracer `db.rs` `first_user_call`), so the step that used to leave the root is no longer taken. Every pinned measurement of this state — the corpus pins, the GPUI window records — is of line 44.
The same frame three statements along: a different line, different locals, different inline values. It is at the laptop viewport so the normalised-rectangle claim has a second width to be wrong at.

A frame entered and RETURNED FROM, which needs the debugger to be TWO frames deep before `stepOut` can land anywhere but the end of the program. MEASURED, 2026-09-21, on the recording itself rather than chosen: `calc`'s module level is a prologue of nine `def` statements and two constants, so step-ins 1..16 never leave `<__main__>`; #17 enters `main` at line 99; #18..#20 walk to the call at line 109; #21 enters `evaluate` at line 72. `stepOut` there returns to `main` at LINE 110, TICK 37. Stepping out one frame shallower — from inside `main` — lands on line 113 at tick 171, which is byte-identical to where `continueForward` lands, and that is what the previous three spellings all did. THE PREVIOUS SPELLING WAS `next x1, stepIn x1, stepOut x1` AND IT COLLIDED: it was validated against a capture that counted CLICKS rather than MOVES, so the recorded corpus was one operation behind and the collision was invisible. Once the capture asserted effect, `returned-calltrace` and `continued-event-log` both reported line 113 at tick 171 — the same screen, reached two ways, which is the population defect (Verification-Harness-Traps §34) this set exists to prevent. The `laptop` viewport is kept as belt and braces but is no longer what carries the distinctness: the two answer sets differed in only two of eight questions when the program state was shared, and both of those two were differences in WINDOW SIZE rather than in anything the debugger did.
Run forward rather than stepped. The recorded event set is the one the program produced, which is the fourth distinct rendering path the methodology asks a tier-1 canary set to cover: a data table.

The only scenario in which the gutter-marks question has a non-empty answer. `line` is relative to the first drawn row and is resolved by each driver against the recording's own source, never against a literal.

gpuiProbes.why: PLAT35-F13 and PLAT35-F14. UNSTEPPED, so the editor's first drawn row is 1 and the frame holds one-digit and two-digit line numbers AT ONCE — which is the only arrangement in which a gutter lane whose cell index moves with the digit count can be seen to collide. `breakpoint-editor` cannot show it (five stepIns put the first drawn row at 31, so its mark always lands on a two-digit row), and before this entry existed the collision was only ever reproduced from an ad-hoc `--replay-ops=setBreakpoint@1` command line. Measured there on 2026-10-03 at 1440x900: line 1 [' ','▶',' ','1'], line 2 [' ',' ','●','2'], line 10 [' ',' ','1','0'] — the dot and the tens digit both at cell index 2. `laptop` because that is where the editor pane is narrowest (276px at 1440) and the gutter's width costs the most.
